name: Variable length arm for Round-a-mount (RAM) mounting system

captions.detailed: This 3D model is a parametric connecting arm designed for a RAM mount system, featuring two hemispherical cup joints on either end connected by a flat, chamfered central bar. Each cup joint has a hollowed-out spherical socket to grip a rubberized ball, along with cutout slots at the outer tips to allow flexibility and clamping range. Two vertical bolt holes are positioned near the transition from the central arm to the cup joints, allowing the clamping force to be secured with fasteners.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric RAM mount arm in OpenSCAD with adjustable length, optional hexagonal nut traps, and configurable bolt holes. The user should be able to specify the arm length, choose between one or two bolt holes, select the bolt standard (such as M4, M5, M6, M8, or 1/4 inch), and toggle the inclusion of a hexagonal nut trap.
captions.factory: The design is built within a `difference()` block. The outer shape is a `union()` of two outer spheres at the ends and a central connecting arm created by rotating a `cube` by 45 degrees. From this base, the script subtracts interior hollows using smaller spheres, shaves off the top and bottom using large flat `cube` primitives, and subtracts the bolt holes. The bolt holes are created using a custom helper module `makeBoltHole()` which selects the appropriate `cylinder` radius and optionally adds a hexagonal nut trap using a custom `hexagon` module composed of rotated cubes.
